name: Priya Sharma
family_history: Coronary Artery Disease (father, fatal MI at 58)

visits.chief_complaint: Fatigue, weight gain despite dieting, cold intolerance
visits.doctor_notes: TSH significantly elevated. Cholesterol profile unfavourable — likely secondary to hypothyroidism. Levothyroxine initiated. Repeat TFTs in 6 weeks. Dietary advice given.

visits.chief_complaint: Palpitations, occasional chest tightness on exertion
visits.diagnosis: Borderline hypertension. Palpitations — likely stress-related, no arrhythmia on ECG.

lab_results.ECG: Normal sinus rhythm. No ST changes.

visits.doctor_notes: Thyroid now controlled. Cholesterol remains high — may need statin if lifestyle measures fail. Blood pressure creeping up. Palpitations attributed to stress and caffeine. Advised reduction in caffeine. Stress ECG within normal limits.

visits.chief_complaint: Chest tightness during stair climbing, shortness of breath
visits.diagnosis: Suspected exertional angina. Hypertension Stage 1. Dyslipidaemia.

lab_results.ECG: T-wave flattening in lateral leads. No acute ST elevation.

visits.doctor_notes: Exertional chest tightness is concerning given family history of CAD. ECG shows non-specific T-wave changes. Troponin negative — no acute event. Statin and aspirin initiated. Cardiology referral for stress echocardiogram. High cardiovascular risk profile.

visits.chief_complaint: Emergency: sudden severe chest pain radiating to left arm
visits.diagnosis: NSTEMI — Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction. Hypertension uncontrolled.

lab_results.ECG: ST depression in V4-V6. T-wave inversion in lateral leads.
lab_results.Echo: EF 48%. Mild hypokinesia in lateral wall.

visits.doctor_notes: NSTEMI confirmed. Troponin significantly elevated. Urgent cardiology intervention. Coronary angiogram planned. The 4-year trajectory — rising BP, LDL, exertional symptoms, T-wave changes — was predictive of this event. Dual antiplatelet therapy initiated. ICU observation post-intervention.
